stem: A 71-year-old man with a history of permanent atrial fibrillation who discontinued his oral apixaban 2 weeks ago presents to the emergency department with sudden-onset, severe pain in his left leg that began 3 hours ago. He states that his left foot feels completely numb and cold. On physical examination, the left lower extremity is pale and marble-cool from the mid-calf down to the toes. Neurological examination of the left foot demonstrates absent sensation to light touch and pinprick over the dorsum and plantar surface, and inability to wiggle his toes or dorsiflex the ankle. Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses are absent to palpation and non-audible on Doppler examination, while the popliteal and femoral pulses are bounding (2+). stem: A 34-year-old woman with a history of Graves disease who has been non-compliant with methimazole presents to the emergency department with severe agitation, confusion, and palpitations 24 hours after undergoing an uncomplicated tooth extraction. On arrival, she is tremulous, delirious, and profusely diaphoretic. Vital signs are: blood pressure 168/76 mm Hg, heart rate 158/min (irregularly irregular, consistent with atrial fibrillation), respiratory rate 26/min, and core temperature 40.2°C (104.4°F). Physical examination reveals marked exophthalmos, a diffusely enlarged non-tender thyroid goiter with an audible systolic bruit, diffuse bibasilar pulmonary crackles, and a 2+ bilateral pretibial pitting edema. Laboratory testing demonstrates an undetectable TSH (< 0.01 microU/mL) and free T4 of 5.8 ng/dL. The Burch-Wartofsky Point Scale score is 65, confirming thyroid storm. Which of the following represents the correct sequence and pharmacotherapy required for this patient?

options.text: Administer high-dose Lugol iodine solution immediately, followed 2 hours later by propylthiouracil and levothyroxine
options.explanation: Administering inorganic iodine before thionamide blockade provides rich iodide substrate to the hyperactive thyroid gland, synthesizing massive amounts of new thyroid hormone and worsening thyroid storm.

options.text: Administer intravenous radioiodine (I-131) ablation therapy immediately to destroy hyperactive thyroid follicular cells
options.explanation: Radioactive iodine ablation in acute thyroid storm causes radiation thyroiditis, releasing stored thyroid hormones into the bloodstream and triggering fatal cardiovascular collapse.

options.text: Administer intravenous amiodarone infusion to convert atrial fibrillation to normal sinus rhythm
options.explanation: Amiodarone contains 37% iodine by weight and is heavily metabolized to release massive iodine loads, worsening thyrotoxicosis and inducing refractory arrhythmias in Graves disease.

options.text: Initiate immediate therapeutic plasma exchange as first-line monotherapy without antithyroid medications
options.explanation: Plasmapheresis is a third-line rescue therapy reserved strictly for patients refractory to full medical management or with severe thionamide-induced agranulocytosis or hepatotoxicity.

options.text: Administer intravenous propranolol, followed by propylthiouracil, followed 1 hour later by potassium iodide (Lugol solution), and intravenous hydrocortisone
options.explanation: Thyroid storm is a life-threatening hypermetabolic state requiring immediate multimodal pharmacotherapy administered in a strict, specific sequence: (1) Beta-blockers (propranolol IV) to control adrenergic hyperactivity and block peripheral T4-to-T3 conversion; (2) Thionamides (propylthiouracil [PTU] or methimazole) to block new thyroid hormone synthesis via thyroid peroxidase inhibition (PTU also blocks peripheral T4-to-T3 conversion); (3) Inorganic iodine (Lugol solution or saturated solution of potassium iodide [SSKI]) to inhibit thyroid hormone release via the Wolff-Chaikoff effect; and (4) Glucocorticoids (IV hydrocortisone) to reduce peripheral conversion and treat potential relative adrenal insufficiency. CRITICAL PHARMACOLOGIC TIMING: Iodine must be administered AT LEAST 1 HOUR AFTER thionamide therapy; giving iodine first provides additional substrate for thyroid hormone synthesis, exacerbating the storm (Jod-Basedow phenomenon).
